conceptCapsule.title: Power Formulation, Scalar Product & Constant Power Kinematics
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Definition of Power: Power is the time rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. (a) Average Power: $P_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\Delta W}{\Delta t} = \frac{\Delta K}{\Delta t}$. (b) Instantaneous Power: $P = \frac{dW}{dt} = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = F v \cos\theta$. 2. Constant Power Motion: If an engine supplies constant power $P$ from rest: (a) $v(t) = \sqrt{\frac{2Pt}{m}} \propto t^{1/2}$, (b) $s(t) = \sqrt{\frac{8P}{9m}} t^{3/2} \propto t^{3/2}$, (c) $v(s) = \left(\frac{3Ps}{m}\right)^{1/3} \propto s^{1/3}$, and (d) $a(s) \propto s^{-1/3}$. 3. Fluid Stream Pumping: For a nozzle ejecting fluid of density $\rho$ through cross-section $A$ at speed $v$, the kinetic power delivered is $P = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{dm}{dt}\right)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho A v^3$. Doubling the flow speed requires $8$ times the power. 4. Aerodynamic Drag: If drag resistance is $F_{\text{drag}} = c v^2$, the power required to maintain constant speed is $P = F v = c v^3$.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v}, \quad P_{\text{avg}} = \frac{W_{\text{total}}}{\Delta t}, \quad v(t) = \sqrt{\frac{2Pt}{m}}, \quad s(t) \propto t^{3/2}, \quad P_{\text{fluid}} = \frac{1}{2}\rho A v^3$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: Do not confuse uniform acceleration with constant power! When an engine delivers *constant power*, acceleration decreases with time ($a \propto t^{-1/2}$), meaning the vehicle accelerates fastest at low speeds and tapers off. Conversely, for *uniform acceleration* ($a = \text{constant}$), power increases linearly with time ($P(t) = m a^2 t \propto t$).

questions.statement: A body of mass $m$ accelerates from rest under the action of an engine delivering constant power $P$. The velocity $v$ of the body as a function of time $t$ is proportional to:
questions.solution:
$$P = F v = m v \frac{dv}{dt} \implies \int_0^v v\,dv = \frac{P}{m}\int_0^t dt \implies \frac{v^2}{2} = \frac{P}{m}t \implies v = \sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}} t^{1/2} \propto t^{1/2}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 1, the displacement $s$ of the body from rest as a function of time $t$ is proportional to:
questions.solution:
$$s = \int_0^t v\,dt = \int_0^t \sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}} t^{1/2}\,dt = \sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}}\left(\frac{t^{3/2}}{3/2}\right) \propto t^{3/2}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: An electric motor delivers $P = 2.0\text{ kW}$ of power to lift a water tank of mass $M = 300\text{ kg}$ to a height of $h = 20\text{ m}$. If the efficiency of the motor is $75\%$, the time taken to fill the tank is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Useful work: $W = M g h = 300 \times 10 \times 20 = 60000\text{ J}$.
2. Output power: $P_{\text{out}} = 0.75 \times 2000 = 1500\text{ W}$.
3. Time: $t = \frac{60000}{1500} = 40\text{ s}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A constant force $\vec{F} = (4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})\text{ N}$ acts on a particle moving with an instantaneous velocity $\vec{v} = (2\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k})\text{ m/s}$. The instantaneous power delivered by the force is:
questions.solution:
$$P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = (4)(2) + (3)(-4) + (-2)(5) = 8 - 12 - 10 = -14\text{ W}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A body of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is projected vertically upwards with an initial speed $u = 20\text{ m/s}$. The instantaneous power delivered by the gravitational force at time $t = 1\text{ s}$ is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Speed at $t = 1\text{ s}$: $v = u - gt = 20 - 10(1) = 10\text{ m/s}$ (upward).
2. Force of gravity: $F_g = mg = 20\text{ N}$ (downward).
3. Power: $P = \vec{F}_g \cdot \vec{v} = -(20)(10) = -200\text{ W}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: An engine pumps water continuously through a pipe of cross-sectional area $A$. If water emerges with a speed $v$, and the density of water is $\rho$, the rate at which work is done by the engine to maintain this flow is:
questions.solution:
Mass flowing per unit time: $\frac{dm}{dt} = \rho A v$.
$$P = \frac{dK}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{dm}{dt}\right)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho A v^3$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: To increase the flow velocity of water in Question 6 by a factor of $2$ ($v' = 2v$), the power delivered by the engine must be increased by a factor of:
questions.solution:
Since $P \propto v^3$, doubling $v$ yields $P' = (2)^3 P = 8P$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: An automobile of mass $m$ accelerates uniformly from rest to speed $v_0$ in time $t_0$. The instantaneous power delivered by the engine at time $t$ ($t \le t_0$) is:
questions.solution:
Acceleration $a = \frac{v_0}{t_0}$. Force $F = ma = \frac{m v_0}{t_0}$.
Speed at time $t$: $v(t) = a t = \frac{v_0}{t_0}t$.
$$P(t) = F v(t) = \left(\frac{m v_0}{t_0}\right)\left(\frac{v_0}{t_0}t\right) = \frac{m v_0^2}{t_0^2} t$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 8, the average power delivered by the engine over the entire interval from $t = 0$ to $t = t_0$ is:
questions.solution:
$$P_{\text{avg}} = \frac{W_{\text{total}}}{t_0} = \frac{\frac{1}{2}m v_0^2}{t_0} = \frac{m v_0^2}{2t_0}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A car of mass $M = 1000\text{ kg}$ climbs an incline of $1$ in $20$ ($\sin\theta = 0.05$) at a constant speed of $v = 15\text{ m/s}$. If the resistance to motion due to friction is $f = 200\text{ N}$, the power developed by the engine is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Net force needed: $F = Mg\sin\theta + f = 1000(10)(0.05) + 200 = 500 + 200 = 700\text{ N}$.
2. Power: $P = F v = 700 \times 15 = 10500\text{ W} = 10.5\text{ kW}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ moves in a straight line such that its displacement $x$ depends on time $t$ as $x = \alpha t^3 + \beta t$. The instantaneous power delivered to the particle is proportional to:
questions.solution:
$v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 3\alpha t^2 + \beta$. $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = 6\alpha t$.
$$P = F v = (m a)v = (6m\alpha t)(3\alpha t^2 + \beta) \propto (3\alpha t^2 + \beta)t$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A vehicle of mass $m$ starts from rest and moves with constant power $P$. The velocity $v$ acquired after travelling a distance $s$ is:
questions.solution:
$$P = F v = \left(m v \frac{dv}{ds}\right)v = m v^2 \frac{dv}{ds} \implies \int_0^v v^2\,dv = \frac{P}{m}\int_0^s ds \implies \frac{v^3}{3} = \frac{P s}{m} \implies v = \left(\frac{3Ps}{m}\right)^{1/3}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves along the $x$-axis from rest at $x = 0$ under a constant power source. The acceleration $a$ of the particle as a function of its displacement $x$ is proportional to:
questions.solution:
From $v \propto x^{1/3}$: $a = v\frac{dv}{dx} = (x^{1/3})\left(\frac{1}{3}x^{-2/3}\right) \propto x^{-1/3}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A crane lifts a load of mass $M = 500\text{ kg}$ vertically upward with a constant acceleration $a = 2\text{ m/s}^2$. The instantaneous power developed by the crane motor at $t = 3\text{ s}$ after starting from rest is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Tension: $T = M(g + a) = 500(10 + 2) = 6000\text{ N}$.
2. Speed at $t = 3\text{ s}$: $v = at = 2 \times 3 = 6\text{ m/s}$.
3. Power: $P = T v = 6000 \times 6 = 36000\text{ W} = 36\text{ kW}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: An elevator cabin of mass $M = 1800\text{ kg}$ is moving upward at a constant speed $v = 3\text{ m/s}$ against a constant frictional resistance force $f = 4000\text{ N}$. The minimum horsepower (hp) required from the motor is ($1\text{ hp} = 746\text{ W}, g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Total force: $F = Mg + f = 18000 + 4000 = 22000\text{ N}$.
2. Power: $P = F v = 22000 \times 3 = 66000\text{ W}$.
3. Horsepower: $P_{\text{hp}} = \frac{66000}{746} \approx 88.47\text{ hp} \approx 88.5\text{ hp}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A machine gun fires $N$ bullets per second, each of mass $m$ with muzzle speed $u$. The power delivered by the gun mechanism to fire the bullets is:
questions.solution:
$$P = \frac{\text{Total Kinetic Energy}}{\Delta t} = N\left(\frac{1}{2}m u^2\right) = \frac{1}{2} N m u^2$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The power supplied to a particle of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ varies with time as $P(t) = 3t^2\text{ W}$. If the particle was initially at rest at $t = 0$, its velocity at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Work done: $W = \int_0^2 3t^2\,dt = [t^3]_0^2 = 8\text{ J}$.
2. Work-Energy Theorem: $\frac{1}{2}(2)v^2 = 8 \implies v^2 = 8 \implies v = 2\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A wind turbine with blades sweeping an area $A$ is placed in a wind stream of speed $v$. If the air density is $\rho$, the maximum theoretical power of the incoming wind stream is:
questions.solution:
$$P = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{dm}{dt}\right)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(\rho A v)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho A v^3$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a circle of radius $R$ with uniform speed $v$. The instantaneous power delivered by the net centripetal force is:
questions.solution:
Because centripetal force is always perpendicular to instantaneous velocity ($\vec{F}_c \cdot \vec{v} = 0$), power delivered is identically zero.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A car travels with constant speed $v$ along a horizontal road where resistive aerodynamic drag is $F_{\text{drag}} = c v^2$. The engine power output required to maintain this speed is proportional to:
questions.solution:
$$P = F_{\text{engine}} v = (c v^2)v = c v^3 \propto v^3$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.
